data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves are attached at the same node, visible in multiple images, with 3–5 leaves per node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely at the apex of the stem, with no clear spacing between nodes)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf is a single blade without subdivisions)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A (leaf complexity is simple)

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth with no teeth or lobes)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): elliptic (broadest near the middle, tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is gently curved, not tapering or lobed)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, closely spaced, 5–7 pairs per leaf (clearly visible in close-up images, forming a distinct network)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (surface has a glossy appearance, reflecting light)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or fuzz on leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petiole is less than 1 cm, connecting leaf to stem)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (circular in cross-section, not flattened or winged)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem appears firm and slightly thickened, typical of young tree seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on stem)
    19. Stem color: green to reddish-brown (young stem is greenish, turning reddish-brown toward base)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no ridges or lenticels visible)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules observed at leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no exudate visible when stem is broken or damaged)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base visible)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no modified stems or leaves forming tendrils)

F. Notes: [NOTE] The seedling exhibits a whorled arrangement of simple, elliptic leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. Leaves are clustered at the shoot apex. Some minor damage is visible on leaf margins (small holes and edge notches), but no clear signs of insect or pathogen activity are present. The stem is smooth and green to reddish-brown, consistent with a young woody seedling. All observations are based on visible traits in the provided images; no family, genus, or species is inferred. The presence of a pink tag and plastic bag suggests field sampling context, but these are not part of the morphological assessment.
